Research

My research focuses on efficient hardware for Edge AI: bringing deep learning inference to devices where power, memory, latency, and compute resources are limited.

Research Focus

  • Low-power AI hardware accelerator architectures
  • Algorithm–hardware co-design and mixed-precision computing
  • VLSI circuit and system design for high-performance digital architectures
  • Physical design automation and RTL-to-GDSII implementation
  • EDA flows and optimization for ASIC and FPGA platforms

PhD Thesis

Design and Implementation of a Reconfigurable Accelerator Architecture for Edge AI Systems

The work combines quantization-aware training, structured pruning, approximate computing, SIMD/CORDIC architectures, and runtime precision scaling to reduce energy and compute complexity while preserving useful model accuracy.

Technical Direction

I work across the full path from algorithm selection and numerical representation to RTL implementation, FPGA validation, physical design, timing closure, and power analysis.
